title: Could the be our frontrunner for Best Musical?  Let’s talk about it! ...
transcript: So I got to attend the first preview of The Notebook on Broadway this past weekend, and I wanna give my thoughts now. Because this was a first preview, I'm not going to do a full review or give it a star rating. I'm mostly just gonna give you my first impression of the material. I guess I'll start with what everyone is probably most curious about, which is the score by Ingrid Michaelson. And I have to say, I really loved the score of this one. It is very Ingrid Michaelson. So if you like Ingrid Michaelson's music, I think you're really gonna like the score of the show. But the flip side is true too. If you don't like Ingrid Michaelson's music, I don't know if the show will be for you. But I am a big ignore Michaelson fan, so I really liked the score, particularly the music, which I thought was gorgeous. I definitely think the lyrics get a bit repetitive at times, but for me it mostly worked for what it was trying to do. And as for the rest of the show, I thought this was in amazing shape for a first preview. Like, we had one technical hold in Act 2, but aside from that, everything moved surprisingly smoothly. And let me tell you, this show moves. It is surprisingly fast paced, and it is constantly moving from one scene to another really, really quickly, which I really appreciate it. I never felt Like the story dragged or that I was bored. I was constantly engaged with what was going on in the show. And the design work is really excellent here. I really like to be set and lighting design and how it all worked together. The set in particular is pretty simple, but also pretty effective. I thought it was perfect for what they needed it to be. It's a really tough show to design for because it is part memory play. There are so many different locations in the show, and I thought that Davidson did a great job balancing all of that in one cohesive design. Something I was a little bit worried of going in was the fact that they had three different actors playing each of the main leads. Do you have the younger versions, the middle versions, and the older versions? Actually thought the show did a really good job at balancing all three timelines and also making it clear that this is the same person, just at three different points in their life. Also do a really cool thing where some of the younger actors will show up in the later timelines is kind of echoes of the past. And I found this to be very effective. Was also a storytelling device that's felt distinctly theatrical. Like, that's not something you could do in the movie version or the book version. You can only really do that in the stage version. Oh, yeah. All in All I think the notebook is in incredible shape. It is honestly my favorite new musical of the season so far, and I really think this will be a contender for Best Musical. So while I'm not gonna give a star rating, I will give you my recommendation to go see the notebook at the show and fell theater.
reasoning: Creator expresses strong enthusiasm throughout, calling it his 'favorite new musical of the season so far' and predicting it will be a 'contender for Best Musical.' Despite being a first preview, he gives a clear recommendation to see the show.
